concepts.name: UNESCO ICH Recognition of Yoga: Year, Category, and Process
key_dimensions: Yoga inscribed on UNESCO Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2016 (NOT 2015 when IDY was declared)
Distinction between UNESCO ICH inscription vs. UNESCO World Heritage (tangible) — common trap
Nomination submitted by India under the 2003 UNESCO Convention for Safeguarding ICH
Yoga listed under the domain 'knowledge and practices concerning nature and the universe'

concepts.name: International Day of Yoga (IDY): Origin, Date, and UN Resolution
key_dimensions: June 21 declared as IDY by UN General Assembly via Resolution 69/131 in December 2014
India's proposal championed by PM Narendra Modi at UNGA — first IDY celebrated on June 21, 2015
June 21 significance: Summer Solstice — longest day in Northern Hemisphere, yogic tradition link
Record co-sponsorship: 177 nations co-sponsored the resolution — one of the highest in UNGA history

concepts.name: 2003 UNESCO Convention for Safeguarding Intangible Cultural Heritage: Structure and Domains
key_dimensions: Five domains: oral traditions, performing arts, social practices, knowledge about nature/universe, traditional craftsmanship
Yoga falls under 'knowledge and practices concerning nature and the universe' — NOT performing arts (trap)
Three lists under the Convention: Representative List, Urgent Safeguarding List, Best Safeguarding Practices Register
India's ratification of the 2003 Convention and its obligations as a State Party

concepts.name: Definition and Philosophical Roots of Yoga as ICH
key_dimensions: Yoga derived from Sanskrit root 'Yuj' meaning to unite/yoke — union of individual consciousness with universal
Origins in Indus Valley civilization, formalized in Vedic texts, Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita, and Patanjali's Yoga Sutras
Yoga as both physical discipline AND philosophical-spiritual system — UNESCO recognized the holistic dimension
Distinction between yoga as ICH (living tradition, community practice) vs. yoga as tangible heritage

concepts.name: Patanjali's Ashtanga Yoga: The Eight Limbs and UPSC Relevance
key_dimensions: Eight limbs: Yama, Niyama, Asana, Pranayama, Pratyahara, Dharana, Dhyana, Samadhi
Patanjali's Yoga Sutras (~2nd century BCE) as the foundational codification of Classical Yoga
Asana is only ONE of eight limbs — UNESCO recognition encompasses the entire system, not just physical postures
Relevance to debates on 'secularism' — yoga as cultural heritage vs. religious practice distinction

concepts.name: Types/Schools of Yoga and Their Textual Basis
key_dimensions: Jnana Yoga (Upanishads), Bhakti Yoga (Bhagavata Purana), Karma Yoga (Bhagavad Gita), Raja Yoga (Patanjali)
Hatha Yoga — 'Hatha Yoga Pradipika' (15th century) by Swatmarama — physical/tantric tradition
Kundalini, Iyengar, Ashtanga Vinyasa — modern derivatives; distinction from classical yoga
Relevance to UNESCO inscription: India nominated yoga as a living, evolving, multi-school tradition

concepts.name: India's Other UNESCO ICH Inscriptions: Comparison and Overlap Traps
key_dimensions: India has 14 elements on UNESCO Representative ICH List (as of 2023) — Yoga (2016), Kumbh Mela (2017), Durga Puja (2021), Garba (2023), etc.
Kumbh Mela inscribed 2017 — same domain 'social practices, rituals and festive events' (trap: different domain from Yoga)
Navroz (2016, multinational) — India a co-nominating country; distinction from solo nominations
Vedic chanting inscribed in 2008 under older 'Proclamation of Masterpieces' — later integrated into 2003 Convention list

concepts.name: Yoga and Indian Soft Power / Cultural Diplomacy
key_dimensions: UNESCO ICH status leveraged as instrument of Indian soft power — 'Brand India' globally
Ministry of AYUSH created in 2014 — nodal ministry for promotion of yoga internationally
Morarji Desai National Institute of Yoga — apex body under AYUSH for yoga research and promotion
Controversy: concerns from some nations about cultural appropriation vs. India's position on yoga as 'universal heritage'

concepts.name: Ministry of AYUSH and Institutional Framework for Yoga
key_dimensions: AYUSH: Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, Homeopathy — constituted as separate Ministry in November 2014
Common Yoga Protocol (CYP) — standardized sequence developed for IDY celebrations globally
Central Council for Research in Yoga and Naturopathy (CCRYN) — research body under AYUSH
National Ayush Mission — integrates yoga into public health delivery at grassroots level

concepts.name: Yoga, Secularism, and Constitutional Debates in India
key_dimensions: Supreme Court rulings: Yoga in schools not a violation of secularism if non-religious components taught (Kerala HC, various rulings)
Article 28 of Constitution — no religious instruction in state-funded schools — yoga's status as cultural vs. religious practice
Controversy over mandatory yoga in schools — Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25-28) dimensions
UNESCO's own framing: emphasized yoga's 'non-denominational' and 'universally accessible' character in inscription

concepts.name: Yoga and Intellectual Property: Patent and Trademark Controversies
key_dimensions: US Patent Office granted yoga-related patents in early 2000s — India's vigorous opposition and Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL)
TKDL: database of 900+ yoga postures in digital format submitted to international patent offices to prevent biopiracy
WIPO and TKDL interface — India's model cited globally for protecting traditional knowledge
UNESCO ICH status strengthens but does NOT automatically grant IP protection — important distinction

concepts.name: Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL) and Protection of Yoga Heritage
key_dimensions: TKDL established 2001 — joint initiative of CSIR and Ministry of AYUSH (then AYUSH dept.)
Documented 3.6 lakh medicinal formulations and 900 yoga asanas from classical texts
TKDL Access Agreement signed with international patent offices (EPO, USPTO, etc.) — defensive publication strategy
Distinction: TKDL protects from misappropriation; UNESCO ICH promotes living practice — two complementary mechanisms

concepts.name: Yoga in Health Policy: AYUSH Integration and WHO Benchmarks
key_dimensions: WHO Benchmarks for Training in Yoga (2023) — first global standards for yoga practice and training safety
National AYUSH Mission integrates yoga therapy into primary healthcare — NHM framework
Yoga included in National Education Policy 2020 as part of holistic health and physical education
Research on yoga's evidence base — ICMR studies on yoga for non-communicable diseases (NCDs)

concepts.name: Criteria for UNESCO ICH Inscription: How Yoga Qualified
key_dimensions: Five criteria under Operational Directives of 2003 Convention: community identification, visibility, dialogue, safeguarding measures, inventory inclusion
India demonstrated yoga as a 'living heritage' with active community transmission across gurus, gurukuls, and institutions
Intergenerational transmission — key criterion: yoga transmitted through guru-shishya parampara
Yoga's inscription noted its 'non-exclusive' nature — practiced across castes, genders, religions globally

concepts.name: Difference Between UNESCO Representative List and Urgent Safeguarding List
key_dimensions: Representative List: promotes visibility of ICH, encourages dialogue — yoga inscribed here (NOT urgent safeguarding)
Urgent Safeguarding List: for ICH requiring immediate measures for survival — e.g., Kalbelia folk songs
Common UPSC trap: assuming that UNESCO ICH inscription means the element is 'endangered' — Representative List does NOT imply threat
Best Practices Register: third list — for programs/projects that best reflect the Convention's principles

concepts.name: Multinational vs. Solo ICH Nominations: India's Yoga as Solo Nomination
key_dimensions: Yoga nominated solely by India — despite being practiced globally, India asserted it as originating Indian tradition
Contrast with Navroz (co-nominated by India + multiple countries) and Kumbh Mela (solo nomination)
Political sensitivity: some Middle Eastern and Western nations practice yoga — question of sole ownership vs. shared heritage
UNESCO's 2003 Convention allows multinational nominations to recognize shared heritage — India's strategic choice to go solo

concepts.name: Guru-Shishya Parampara as Transmission Mechanism for Yoga ICH
key_dimensions: UNESCO ICH emphasizes 'intergenerational transmission' — guru-shishya parampara as primary vehicle for yoga
Institutionalization: from traditional gurukuls to modern yoga institutes (BKS Iyengar, Pattabhi Jois, Sivananda lineages)
Digital and diaspora transmission — challenge and opportunity for safeguarding authenticity
UNESCO inscription recognizes community-based transmission, not just institutional/commercial yoga

concepts.name: Yoga vs. Ayurveda in UNESCO and International Recognition: Comparison
key_dimensions: Yoga: inscribed on UNESCO ICH Representative List (2016); Ayurveda: NOT yet inscribed on UNESCO ICH list — important trap
Ayurveda covered under TKDL and WHO Traditional Medicine Strategy 2014-2023, but lacks UNESCO ICH status
Both under Ministry of AYUSH — students often conflate their international recognition status
India has nominated Ayurveda for UNESCO ICH — process ongoing as of knowledge cutoff

concepts.name: Common Examiner Traps: Yoga-Related Facts Frequently Confused
key_dimensions: Trap 1: IDY declared in 2014 (UNGA resolution) but first celebrated in 2015 — year confusion common
Trap 2: Yoga inscribed in 2016 NOT 2015 (year IDY was first held)
Trap 3: UNESCO ICH inscription is on 'Representative List' NOT 'World Heritage List' (tangible heritage)
Trap 4: UNGA Resolution 69/131 declared IDY — NOT UNESCO; UNESCO inscribed yoga separately two years later

concepts.name: Yoga and National Education Policy 2020: Curricular Integration
key_dimensions: NEP 2020 explicitly mentions yoga as part of health, physical education, and well-being across all school stages
Bagless days concept under NEP includes yoga, arts, crafts — holistic education framework
Integration of AYUSH including yoga in medical education — AYUSH practitioners given expanded roles
NEP's emphasis on Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS) — yoga positioned as flagship IKS element
